q: 1. To avoid any possibility of tension occurring in masonry structures, the resultant of various forces at any level must through
options: middle third of the width or depth of the section
explain: The 'middle third rule' requires the resultant force to pass within the middle third of the section width/depth to prevent tensile stress in masonry (which cannot resist tension).

q: 2. Force is the product of
explain: According to Newton's Second Law, $F = m \cdot a$.

q: 3. The function of king post in a roof truss is
options: to support the framework of the roof
to receive the ends of principal rafters
to prevent the walls from spreading outward
to prevent the tie beam from sagging at its centre
explain: The king post is a central vertical member that supports the tie beam below it, preventing it from sagging due to its own weight.

q: 4. The effective length of a column with both ends hinged is
explain: For a column hinged (pinned) at both ends, the effective length equals the actual length: Le = L.

q: 5. The effective length of a column with one end fixed and the other end free is
explain: For a column fixed at one end and free at the other, the effective length is Le = 2L.

q: 6. Which of the following is a true example of a statically determinate beam?
options: one end is fixed and the other end is simply supported
the beam over hangs over two support
the beam is supported on three supports
explain: An overhanging beam with two supports has three reaction components, which can be solved with three equilibrium equations.

q: 7. A rigid jointed plane frame is stable and statically determinate ............. .
explain: For a rigid-jointed plane frame (each joint with 3 dof), the condition for stable and statically determinate structure is 3m + r = 3j.

q: 8. The number of independent equations to be satisfied for static equilibrium in a space structure is
explain: A three-dimensional (space) structure requires 6 independent equilibrium equations: 3 force equations (ΣFx, ΣFy, ΣFz) and 3 moment equations (ΣMx, ΣMy, ΣMz).

q: 9. The degree of static indeterminacy of a pin jointed space frame is given by
explain: For a pin-jointed space frame, each joint has 3 equilibrium equations (3D translation), giving static indeterminacy Ds = m + r − 3j.

q: 10. The degree of kinematic indeterminacy of a pin jointed space frame is
explain: Each joint of a pin-jointed space frame has 3 possible translational displacements, so kinematic indeterminacy = 3j − r (subtracting restrained reaction components).

q: 11. The number of independent displacement components at each joint of a rigid jointed space frame is
explain: A rigid joint in 3D space can have 3 translations and 3 rotations, giving 6 independent displacement components per joint.

q: 12. For finding forces in the members of truss by the graphical method, the force diagram is suggested by
explain: The graphical method of truss analysis using a combined force/stress diagram (Maxwell diagram) for finding member forces was developed by Maxwell.

q: 13. In a pin jointed plane frame all the loads are assumed to act .............
options: in the plane of the frame
perpendicular to the plane of the frame
in a plane inclined at 45° to the plane of frame
explain: For a plane (2D) pin-jointed frame, loads are, by definition of the idealization, assumed to act within the plane of the frame.

q: 14. The deflection at any point of a perfect frame can be obtained by applying a unit load at the joint in
options: the direction in which the deflection is required
explain: The unit load method (virtual work) requires the unit load to be applied at the point and in the exact direction of the deflection being sought.

q: 15. For analyzing pin jointed frames by method of joints; the number of equations of static equilibrium available is
explain: At each pin joint of a plane truss, only 2 equilibrium equations are available (ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0), since moment equilibrium is automatically satisfied at a pin.

q: 16. For analyzing pin jointed frames by method of joints, the joints must be selected in succession such that
options: only two members meet at that joint
only three members meet at that joint
only two unknown forces exist at that point
there is no external forces acting in the joint
explain: The method of joints requires proceeding to joints where only 2 unknown member forces remain, since only 2 equilibrium equations are available per joint to solve them.

q: 17. For analyzing pin jointed frames by method of sections, the section should be so chosen that it cuts
options: only three members at a time
any number of members but only two members with unknown forces
any number of members but only three members with unknown forces
explain: The method of sections uses 3 equilibrium equations (ΣFx, ΣFy, ΣM), so a cutting section should pass through at most 3 members with unknown forces to be solvable.

q: 18. In a rigid jointed frame, the rotation of various members meeting at a joint will be
options: proportional to the length of member
proportional to respective moment of inertia
explain: Since a rigid joint rotates as a single unit, all members rigidly connected at that joint undergo the same (equal) angle of rotation.

q: 19. The displacements of a truss can be obtained directly from
explain: The Williot-Mohr diagram is a specific graphical method used to directly determine joint displacements of a truss.

q: 20. The basic form of a pin jointed frame is
explain: A triangle is the only basic polygon shape that is inherently rigid (stable) when pin-jointed, making it the fundamental unit of truss construction.

q: 21. In a pin jointed plane frame, all the loads will be assumed to act at .............
options: only on the top chords joints
explain: For a truss to be analyzed with members carrying only axial forces, loads must be idealized as acting only at the joints (pins), not along member lengths.

q: 22. By assuming that all the forces acting on a pin connected truss are co planar and act at a joint only it can be expected that all the member will be subjected to
options: direct stress and shear stress only
explain: With loads applied only at joints (pins) and members assumed weightless/straight, truss members carry only direct (axial) stress — either tension or compression, with no bending or shear.

q: 23. In a pin jointed frame, it is sufficient if the forces in all the members meeting at a joint are .............
explain: For equilibrium at a pin joint (which cannot resist moment), it suffices that all member forces meeting there are coplanar and concurrent (passing through the same point).

q: 24. A truss containing j joints and m members, will be a simple truss if
explain: The standard condition for a statically determinate (simple) truss relates members and joints as m = 2j − 3 (accounting for 3 reaction components).

q: 25. A compound truss may be formed by connecting two simple rigid frames by
options: three bars intersecting at a point
explain: Two simple rigid (stable) truss units can be combined into a stable compound truss by connecting them with exactly three non-parallel, non-concurrent bars.

q: 26. m1 and m2 are the members of two individual simple trusses of a compound truss. The compound truss will be rigid and determinate if
explain: Since three additional connecting bars are needed to join two simple trusses into a stable compound truss, the total member count becomes m = m1 + m2 + 3.

q: 27. The forces in the members of simple trusses, may be analysed by
explain: Truss member forces can be determined by any of the graphical method, method of joints, or method of sections — all are valid standard techniques.

q: 28. If two force acting at a joint are not along the straight line, then for the equilibrium of the joint
options: one of the forces must be zero
forces must be equal and of the same sign
forces must be equal in magnitude but opposite in sign
explain: If two non-collinear forces act at a joint with no other forces, equilibrium (ΣF=0 in two independent directions) can only be satisfied if both forces are individually zero.

q: 29. A member is balanced at its end by two inclined members carrying equal forces, equilibrium the angle between the inclined bars must be
explain: For two equal-force inclined members to balance a load symmetrically at a joint with no other member, the resultant condition for equilibrium requires the two members to be at 120° to each other (each at 60° to the load line).

q: 30. A column with maximum equivalent length has
options: one end fixed and the other end hinged
one end fixed and the other end free
explain: A column with one end fixed and the other completely free has the largest effective length (Le = 2L), the maximum among the standard end conditions.
